title: Ongoing Reflections On The Crypto Market
content:
Early november 2025;

Another massive red day; I had closed every position already, just had some GNO left for cashback on gnosis pay, that I ended up selling too. 

3 november 25 is the first day in a while where I don't have long (spot) positions in the crypto market (outside stables). 

Watching all of this unfold from the sidelines, for better or for worse.

**Where do we stand now**

It is bizarre that we've come to expect that retail will come once every four years like clockwork to get scalped. And even more bizarre is the fact that some still pretend that there was neither massive retail presence nor the euphoria that accompanies it during this cycle. 

First, retail was there in full swing during the memecoin meta; they provided the liquidity for the BONK, POPCAT, WIF's of this cycle. The absolute peak of WIF was in March 24; more than 1.5 years ago. 

There was massive euphoria in the memecoin casino, for at least one year between early 2024 (when WIF starts gaining momentum) and early 2025 (Trump memecoin, massive extraction event, pico-top for the memecoin mania, market remained flat for the remainder of the year).

I think that, in parallel to this mania that was heavily skewed to benefit insiders, what exhausted most participants was that *hype cycles* were getting shorter and shorter. We had the AI meta, we had the perps meta, we had the privacy coin meta, but at no point in time during these waves was there any belief, just market participants pumping the prices and trying to cash-out before the others.

**That's why this bull market *felt* different; there was no belief in the transformative power of blockchain as a technology, just the common agreement that this tool could be very efficient to try and make a quick buck.** 

No "chinese ethereum" this time, no Mashinsky sporting a 'banks are not your friends' tshirt, only cynicism and USD-denominated dreams. 

**There simply cannot be a prolonged bull market with zero belief in the tech, when most token-holders have their finger on the trigger, ready to dump as soon as the price starts moving in the wrong direction.**

This is especially true in crypto where for most of the projects, there is little to no value accrual to the token when the protocol/app makes any benefits (see the AAVE DAO debacle on the topic of tokens =/= equity), so traditional valuation models (eg. DCF) do not apply, and valuations are driven first and foremost by belief.

On a broader aspect, since 2020-ish, financial nihilism became more and more prevalent in society; betting markets became ubiquitous in the US, equities started ripping like crazy as trading became much easier with platforms like robinhood and heavy market manipulation came directly from the white house. Then silver and gold started ripping too.

In other words, crypto became just one way among many others for retail participants to get some thrills from their smartphone. On top of that, there is no incentive to try and go further along the risk curve investing in crypto when more established assets like gold make parabolic moves and all the sexy nasdaq stocks are reaching new highs.


The 10/10 dump was really the nail in the coffin for the bull market, showing everyone that there is little to no organic liquidity on most altcoins, as they dumped 50%+ when market makers entered panic mode. My opinion, on the first day of 2026, is that **most traders left in the crypto market are trading against gravity now.**

Maybe this is good. I really felt disgusted by the coordinated pump of zcash by influencers at the end of 2025. This industry is rotted to the core. Burn it all to the ground. Maybe the cypherpunk ethos will re-emerge from the ashes, who knows. 

Looking forward, my prediction is that -unfortunately- the market won't capitulate completely before Metamask, Rabby, OpenSea, etc. finally launch their tokens, as powerful actors have an incentive to pump the prices until then. Most probably, this will provide one last exit window for those still left. 

**But then, exiting to what?**

As mentioned, equities are in a crazy hype cycle propelled by AI stocks. I think cash remains king for now. There is maybe some upside left for some crypto tokens, but I'm 100% convinced the music has already stopped. Most of the multiples have already been made, it's too risky to chase even a +20% now. You don't want to be left holding the bag.

So what now? For me, mostly stables on [low-risk defi](https://vitalik.eth.limo/general/2025/09/21/low_risk_defi.html), and maybe some little polymarket bets to still get those little dopamine hits once in a while.

I'll probably start DCA'ing some stETH/rETH on the way down, as I've never been more bullish on the ETH ecosystem (more on that on The Case For ETH Nationalism), but that's all. Time to touch some grass, I guess. 

Milady.
